statement: Start with Claude Opus 5.5 for most workloads. Use Claude Fable 5.2 for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, or when Opus 5.5 at higher effort still falls short in your evals.

Default effort is high. Use medium for interactive coding, chat and everyday knowledge work; xhigh only for the hardest long-running work where a gain has been measured; max to measure the ceiling. Lower the effort level instead of asking the model to think less. Re-run the effort sweep instead of carrying over settings from other models.
Subagents can drive much of a session's cost; check which model they use. Remove standing delegation instructions that are no longer needed.
Gemini 4 Argon remains the better fit for most software engineering and knowledge work. Gemini 4 Carbon uses more tokens to explore hard problems such as complex debugging and open-ended research.

source.title: Google: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available

statement: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is the fast, cost-efficient daily driver for agentic workflows and everyday tasks.

GPT-6.2 Astra is a frontier model for the hardest projects; GPT-6.2 Sol is an efficient, versatile model for everyday work. Vendor: on FrontierCode 2.0, Sol nearly matches Astra on merge-ready changes at about one-fifth the cost.

source.title: OpenAI Developer Community announcement: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are now available

statement: Gemini 4 Neon sits between Gemini 4 Carbon, for the deepest long-horizon projects, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, for rapid everyday execution. In Antigravity, Orchestrator can plan with Neon and implement with Hydrogen.

source.title: Antigravity: Gemini 4 Neon in Google Antigravity
